title: Next.js Production Handbook: Assets, SEO, Config and Deployment
summary: Quick revision notes on next/image, next/font, the Metadata API and SEO, bundle analysis, environment variables, output modes (standalone, static export), and deploying to Vercel or a Node server.

chapters.title: Optimized Assets: next/image and next/font
points: next/image mental model: an <Image> component that resizes, converts to WebP/AVIF, lazy-loads, and reserves space to prevent layout shift (CLS)
Required props: src plus width and height (or fill inside a position:relative parent); static imports (import img from './a.png') supply width, height and blurDataURL automatically
Set priority on the above-the-fold LCP image to preload it; everything else lazy-loads by default; use sizes with responsive or fill images so the browser doesn't download a viewport-wide file
Remote images must be allow-listed in next.config remotePatterns (protocol, hostname, pathname); an unlisted host throws an error at request time

next/font: import from next/font/google or next/font/local; fonts are downloaded at build time and self-hosted, so there are no runtime requests to Google; use the returned className or variable on <html>/<body> and set display: 'swap'

chapters.title: Metadata API and SEO
points: Export a static `metadata` object or an async `generateMetadata({ params })` from a layout.tsx or page.tsx (Server Components only); child segments override and merge with parent metadata
Core fields: title (string or { template: '%s | Site', default }), description, openGraph, twitter, alternates.canonical, robots
Dynamic pages: generateMetadata fetches data; identical fetch calls are deduplicated with the page's own fetch, so there is no double request
File conventions: app/sitemap.ts, app/robots.ts, opengraph-image.tsx, icon.png and favicon.ico are picked up automatically and served at the standard URLs
JSON-LD structured data is not part of metadata: render a <script type='application/ld+json'> tag in the page component

chapters.title: Environment Variables and Bundle Analysis
points: Load order and files: .env, .env.local, .env.development/.env.production (and .env.test); process.env wins over files; .env.local is not loaded in test mode and must stay out of git
Only variables prefixed NEXT_PUBLIC_ are inlined into the client bundle at build time; all others stay server-only and are undefined in the browser
Mistake: NEXT_PUBLIC_ values are frozen at build, so changing them at runtime does nothing without a rebuild; read server-only vars at request time in a dynamic route to pick up runtime values
Bundle analysis: install @next/bundle-analyzer, wrap next.config with withBundleAnalyzer({ enabled: process.env.ANALYZE === 'true' }), run ANALYZE=true next build to open the treemap reports

Fixes for large bundles: next/dynamic or React.lazy for heavy client components, import only the needed functions from libraries, and move work to Server Components so it ships no JS; check the First Load JS column in build output

chapters.title: Output Modes: Default, Standalone and Static Export
points: Default (next build, next start): a Node server that supports SSR, ISR, route handlers, middleware and image optimization
output: 'standalone' in next.config traces needed files into .next/standalone with a minimal server.js and trimmed node_modules; run with node .next/standalone/server.js
Standalone does not copy public/ or .next/static; copy them into the standalone folder (or serve them from a CDN) or assets return 404
output: 'export' emits plain HTML/CSS/JS to the out/ folder with no server; host on any static host or CDN

Static export limits: no SSR or dynamic request-time rendering, no route handlers that read the request, no middleware, no ISR, and the default image loader doesn't work (use unoptimized: true or a custom loader); dynamic routes need generateStaticParams

chapters.title: Deploying to Vercel or a Node Server
points: Vercel: connect the Git repo and every push builds automatically, with preview deployments per branch/PR and production on the main branch; set env vars per environment (Production, Preview, Development) in the dashboard
On Vercel, routes become serverless or edge functions, static assets go to the CDN, and ISR and image optimization are managed with zero config
Self-hosted Node: run next build, then next start -p 3000 (or node .next/standalone/server.js), supervise with PM2 or systemd, and put nginx or a load balancer in front for TLS and gzip
Docker pattern: multi-stage build (deps → build → runner) using the standalone output, run as a non-root user, set PORT and HOSTNAME=0.0.0.0, and expose the port

Self-hosting tradeoffs: you own the image optimization cache (install sharp), the ISR/data cache (shared across multiple instances needs a custom cache handler), and CDN caching of /_next/static; build-time env must be present during next build

chapters.title: Production Cheat Sheet
points: next/image: width and height or fill, priority for LCP, sizes for responsive, remotePatterns for remote hosts
next/font: google or local, build-time self-hosted, apply className to <body>
Metadata: export metadata or generateMetadata; title.template; sitemap.ts and robots.ts; JSON-LD via script tag
Env and analysis: NEXT_PUBLIC_ is build-time and client-visible; ANALYZE=true next build with @next/bundle-analyzer
Output and deploy: default = next start; standalone = node server.js (copy public and .next/static); export = out/ static only; Vercel = push to deploy; Node = PM2 or Docker behind a proxy
